Subject: Discovery recap — multi-tenant controls, rate limits & per-customer routing

Hi Priya / Sam —

Thanks again for your time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the items we agreed to follow up on. Ive focused this note on the multi-tenant controls we discussed (rate limits, quotas, routing/tiering), plus the success criteria you mentioned.

Pain points (customer-stated)
- Lack of per-customer rate limits: one noisy tenant can degrade throughput for others.
- Billing/visibility: their current stack only provides aggregate token counts per cluster; they need tenant-level billing and cost attribution.
- Routing & tiering: need ability to route high-value customers to lower-latency model variants or dedicated capacity and enforce tiered quotas.
- Policy enforcement & audit: compliance needs audit trails for requests and per-tenant policy application.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Fronted by AWS ALB -> internal API gateway -> ECS services.
- Using a mix of OpenAI hosted endpoints and an in-house caching layer for embeddings.
- No formal quota engine today; team relies on ad-hoc limits.

Success criteria (you emphasized)
1) Per-tenant rate limiting (soft + hard) with clear SLA behavior.
2) Tenant-level billing items and token/response telemetry exported to billing system.
3) Policy-driven per-customer routing: e.g., premium tenants routed to dedicated capacity or a faster model variant.
4) Data isolation guarantees (logical separation + audit logs) suitable for a PCI-adjacent workload.
5) Minimal impact to 99th percentile latency — any mitigation should preserve production SLOs.

What Redwood can deliver (summary)
- Route-level token-bucket rate limits with per-tenant configuration and throttling behavior you can tune.
- Quotas enforced in control plane with soft/hard enforcement and hooks for billing exports (CSV / S3 push or webhook).
- Policy engine for routing: route by tenant metadata to model variant, region, or dedicated pool.
- Audit logs + request-level telemetry retained per your retention policy (we can discuss retention windows).
- Deployment options: shared multitenant runtime with strong logical isolation, or Dedicated pools/private deployments for strict isolation.

Immediate next steps (agreed)
- Redwood: produce a short architecture sketch showing tenant isolation modes and an example per-tenant config (rate/quotas/routing). Attachment: discovery-notes-0305.pdf, rate_quota_requirements.xlsx. (Action: Marissa)
- Northbridge: share a short list of top 10 tenants by traffic profile and the expected monthly token budgets for each (Action: Priya).
- Schedule a 45-min follow-up technical session with Aditya + Vivek from Redwood and your infra/security folks; proposed windows next Tue/Wed morning PT. (Action: Sam)

Please see the attached notes for a compact table of the quota buckets we sketched. Im copying Aditya and Rachel to help on the technical and CS follow-ups.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Hi Priya / team — quick technical note answering the two asks you made: tenant-level config example and what "logical separation" covers.

Example tenant config (conceptual)
- tenant_id: nb-premium-01
- rate_limit:
  - type: token_bucket
  - rate: 20rps
  - burst: 100
  - enforcement: soft (429 with X-RateLimit-Reset) / hard (queue reject)
- monthly_quota: 1,200,000 tokens
- routing_policy:
  - preferred_pool: northbridge-premium-pool (dedicated)
  - fallback_pool: shared-fast-fallback
  - model_selector: [gpt-4x-onnx-quant, gpt-4x-8bit]

Notes on isolation & audit
- KV cache: per-tenant namespaces in the cache layer so entries are scoped by tenant_id; eviction and cache capacity can be partitioned or shared with weighted quotas.
- Logs & telemetry: request traces and token-level telemetry are tagged with tenant_id and can be routed to separate S3 prefixes or pushed to your billing webhook. Access to logs is controlled via RBAC; we can produce an ACL matrix for who sees tenant logs.
- Control plane vs runtime: configuration and quotas live in the control plane (customer-specific metadata). Runtime enforces limits and emits events. For strict compliance we recommend either Dedicated pools or Redwood Private (VPC) so the runtime and control plane are isolated to your tenancy.

Routing/tiering behavior
- Policy engine evaluates tenant metadata, request attributes, and current capacity to make routing decisions. You can pin a tenant to a pool (dedicated) or set rules that prefer premium pools and fall back to shared variants.
- We support both model-variant fallback and region-based routing to keep P99 latency under your target.

Attachments: Ive attached a simple diagram (multitenancy-illustration.png) and a short design note link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cExampleDesignDoc

Happy to walk through the config and how it maps to your orchestration — I can demo the policy rules and a live throttling scenario on the call.

Best,
